title: Put back the build's frozen copies of the 16 downloaded emulators (deleted by mistake on 14 October 2026)
why: scripts/fetch-buildbot-cores.sh takes the 16 emulators Continuum downloads (instead of building) from this repository's core-mirror-1 pre-release first: exact copies, checked by sha256, of the files build 121 shipped, so a change at the libretro buildbot can never slip into the app (its header comment, 'FROZEN BY CHECKSUM'). Build 185 took all 17 files (16 zips and prboom.wad) from there. On 14 October the old releases were deleted on the owner's say-so, and core-mirror-1 went with them, because the check before deleting looked for uses of tags and missed this script's download URL. It was re-created empty straight away (same tag, pre-release, so /releases/latest still points at build 185). The deleted zips can't be restored, but nothing is lost: build 185's install (release build-185-393f12c, kept) still holds all 16 emulators exactly as shipped, changed only by the build's own install-name step (so their sha256 no longer equals the dylib pins), and its prboom.wad is byte for byte the pinned file (checked 14 October).
facts: 12 of the 16 still match at the buildbot (the 14 October update check: 'same as ours'), so a build gets the same emulators as before, only without the frozen-copy protection: wonderswan, ngp, pce, supergrafx, puae, dosbox_pure, handy, prosystem, a5200, pokemini, yabause, mednafen_saturn.

4 have moved on at the buildbot, to builds checked and turned down on 12 October (checked_skip in scripts/check-core-updates.sh): prboom (DOOM: default sound and music volume maxed, so it clips), virtualjaguar (about 13% slower), mednafen_vb (Virtual Boy, about 19% slower), vice_x64sc (C64: same code, f63b566, only the build date differs). Until M2 is done, a build would ship those four newer builds (fetch_one keeps a moved core with a ::warning:: and records it as unpinned).
A master build re-uploads a file to the mirror only when the download matches the ZIP pin, and the buildbot re-zips nightly, so the mirror won't refill by itself.

Never change a zip pin to make this work: CORE_BUILDS in crates/emulator-bridge/src/core_updates.rs keys the players' one-time heads-up on it, so a new pin tells players their emulator changed when it didn't.
hard_rules: Every commit ends with [skip ci]. scripts/fetch-buildbot-cores.sh is a build push path.
This job must be complete BEFORE the next build.

items.title: Accept a frozen copy by the emulator file inside it, and refill the mirror for the 12
items.detail: In fetch_pinned's mirror step, when the copy's zip sha256 isn't the pin, unzip it the way fetch_one does and accept it if the dylib inside matches pinned_dylib_sha256 for that core, recorded as pinned: the same rule fetch_one already applies to an upstream download. prboom.wad has no dylib and keeps the zip-only rule. Add checks (next to whatever scripts/check-*.sh already covers this script, or a small new one): an exact zip is accepted; a re-zipped copy of the same dylib is accepted; a different dylib is refused and falls back to upstream; a missing copy falls back to upstream. Then, for each of the 12 cores whose buildbot dylib still matches its dylib pin, upload the buildbot's current zip under the asset name fetch_one asks for: gh release upload core-mirror-1 <file> --repo 2c2bhdhw9z-cell/Continuum- --clobber. Upload prboom.wad if its download matches its pin. Prove each by downloading it back from the mirror and running the new check on it.
items.result: Done 16 October: the mirror accepts a copy by the dylib inside it, a master build uploads anything it had to fetch elsewhere, and scripts/check-core-mirror.sh holds the rules (41 checks). The hand upload was impossible (the sandbox's GitHub gateway refuses release uploads, HTTP 400), so the next master build refills the mirror itself; the 11 the buildbot still serves (puae moved on 15 October) come from there meanwhile.

items.title: DOOM, Jaguar, Virtual Boy and C64: the checked builds
items.detail: Take them from build 185's install (release build-185-393f12c, Continuum-185.ipa): Payload/Continuum.app/Frameworks/<core>_libretro_ios.dylib is the checked build of each, as shipped (versions inside: prboom v2.5.0 e5db549, virtualjaguar v3.6.1 f9a3c89, vice_x64sc 3.10 f63b566; read mednafen_vb's). Zip each under the asset name fetch_one asks for, upload it to core-mirror-1 (--clobber), and set that core's pinned_dylib_sha256 to the file's sha256; leave the zip pins alone (no false heads-up). M1's rule then accepts them. Check that the staging step accepts a dylib whose install name is already @rpath/<name> (it sets the same name) and that the 185 copies pass every staging check. Also upload Payload/Continuum.app/support/prboom.wad from the same install as prboom.wad: it is byte for byte the pinned file. Fallback, only if a 185 copy is refused: build that core from source at the commit above as an optional core in its own recipe region.
items.result: Done 16 October: DOOM, Jaguar, Virtual Boy, C64 and now Amiga (rebuilt at the buildbot on 15 October) are taken from build 185's install by a new fallback in fetch_pinned, their dylib pins are the 185 copies' sha256, zip pins untouched; a full real fetch staged all 16 as pinned with no warning.

items.title: Write it up
items.detail: A short note in .kiro/notes/docs/reports/ (what was lost, what was put back, how it's proven), fold it into the hand-off, set complete to true.
